- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true mean.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.00–0.10) and price is trending down, model underestimates decline; add 2–5% downward bias to next 5–10 days.  
- Model frequently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) reversals; if true outcome shows mean reversion within 3 days, adjust forecast to align with 5–7 day moving average.  
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) and price is falling, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts downward too aggressively; add 1–3% upward bias to next 3–5 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction by 2–5% per day until convergence with true trend.  
- Sentiment history with repeated 0.00 values (neutral) often leads to model drift; use 7-day moving average of true price as anchor for next 10–15 days.
